summary: Re-tested M1-S04 of build tier2-webhook after apex-builder's run-4 (S2-F-12) test-only repair, which replaced classes/TestDataFactory.cls with a verbatim copy of the corrected templates/apex/tests/TestDataFactory.cls. All 4 .cls-meta.xml files parsed at apiVersion 67.0; the manifest check is skipped-not-applicable under the Apex exception, naming build-level manifest step M1-S05; all 3 declared checkers (apex-scheduled-jobs, apex-queueable-patterns, error-handling-framework) exited 0, backed by a passing check-outputs; the 1 declared manual test was checked against the Given/When/Then usability bar and deferred to the milestone gate as usable. results.json passed:true with 0 failed, so the step was moved built -> tested.
confidence_rationale: Every declared test ran or was correctly classified as manual, both always-on checks completed, and every result came from an exit code this agent observed directly (step-tester Plan Step 7).

process_observations.observation: The S2-F-12 repair touched exactly one file (a verbatim template copy) and left both production classes and the test class unchanged, and the checker suite re-ran clean on the first attempt with no follow-up fix needed.
The undeclared due-diligence diff between the shipped TestDataFactory.cls and the canonical template is byte-identical, confirming no drift was introduced by the repair.

A package.xml exists under M1-S01's artefacts, a step M1-S04 depends_on, which could read as satisfying the manifest-check's 'located a package.xml' condition literally; it names only CustomObject and CustomField members (Integration_Failure__c, Tier2_Escalation__e and their fields) with no ApexClass type block at all, so it does not cover M1-S04's derived Apex members and the Apex exception (step type + apex-builder agent) governs instead, exactly as the step's own declared acceptance test expects.

This is the second consecutive test-only repair on M1-S04 (S2-F-11, then S2-F-12) surfaced by a mock-deploy run rather than by a step-level checker, echoing apex-builder's own run-4 envelope note that the library has no static rule for a test factory assigning a lookup argument unconditionally.
milestone:M1 was previously accepted on evidence that now predates two test-level findings (S2-F-11, S2-F-12) across its two Apex steps.
process_observations.followup_reason: because milestone:M1's acceptance predates this repair and its predecessor, a fresh /verify-milestone against a dry run that actually executes tests re-signs that acceptance on current evidence.
